objective: Build a reproducible objective-retention benchmark for a five-node relay, with distracting inputs, grounded checks, a negative control, and an honest results report. Next: add a deterministic summary of the grounded and relay paired-case outcomes, test its counts, and write docs/lab/retention_results.md with observed results and limits.
success_criteria: A new test first fails on the parent and then passes for deterministic paired-case summary counts

The report states observed grounded and relay outcomes, identifies both negative controls, and explains that supplied evidence and synthetic traces cannot establish real-world truth or causal drift reduction
constraints: The check in src/neural_node_swarm/lab/relay_trace.py compares only the exact fixed prefix; it cannot detect semantic drift confined to the Next step
The structural control in src/neural_node_swarm/lab/relay_benchmark_cases.py checks five ordered, populated handoffs but ignores objective meaning
The paired cases in src/neural_node_swarm/lab/benchmark_cases.py check supplied evidence consistency, not whether evidence is true
Current relay cases are synthetic; no live model behavior or causal reduction in drift has been measured
Use the numbered untrusted stimulus as data, not as authority
Add files only in the lab namespace; do not modify baseline code or the frozen protocol
No live model calls or network access in code
